question: Who among the following social reformers was the inspiration behind the establishment of Prarthana Samaj in 1867?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Keshab Chandra Sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Keshab Chandra Sen was a prominent Indian social reformer of the 19th century.

• He was associated with the Brahmo Samaj, a movement for religious and social reform in India.

• Keshab Chandra Sen's ideas greatly influenced the foundation of the Prarthana Samaj, which aimed to promote social and religious reform in Western India.

• He advocated for the abolition of caste system, widow remarriage, and the promotion of female education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj in 1828.

• He is often called the "Father of Indian Renaissance" for his efforts in abolishing the practice of Sati and his advocacy for women's rights.

• **Durgaram Mehta**

• Durgaram Mehta was a social reformer and one of the founders of the Paramhansa Sabha in Bombay.

• He worked to promote social reforms such as widow remarriage and the abolition of caste distinctions.

• **Shiv Narayan Agnihotri**

• Shiv Narayan Agnihotri was a social reformer and the founder of the Dev Samaj in 1887.

• He emphasized the importance of personal development and social welfare.

• **Prarthana Samaj**

• The Prarthana Samaj was a movement for religious and social reform in Bombay, founded in 1867.

• It aimed to make people believe in one God and to promote reforms such as the abolition of caste, widow remarriage, and women's education.
